items.title: ‘Come and invest’ – Lands Minister assures mining investors of reforms and clear rules
items.description: Lands and Natural Resources Minister Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah has called on investors, financiers, technology partners and international development institutions to invest in Ghana, assuring them of the country’s commitment to reforming the management of its mineral wealth while ensuring that its benefits are shared more widely. Speaking at the 2026 Mining in Motion Conference on Monday, 19 October, under the theme ‘One Continent, One Voice on Minerals: Aligning Africa’s Minerals Future’, Mr Buah said Ghana was resetting how it governed its mineral resources and called for partnerships that would support both commercially successful investments and the country’s development priorities. “Let me assure you, Ghana is resetting the way we govern our mineral wealth and how its benefits are shared,” he said. The Minister acknowledged that meaningful reforms would require consultations, adjustments and patience, urging investors and development partners to remain engaged as the process progressed. He said Ghana was committed to providing a predictable investment environment characterised by clear rules, fair administration, open dialogue and respect for lawful agreements. “I ask for your understanding and constructive engagement as this work moves forward. In return, we should expect clear rules, fair administration, open dialogue, and respect for lawful agreements. That is what Ghana stands for,” he said. Mr Buah stressed that investment certainty remained important to attracting capital, noting that mining projects needed to be commercially viable and capable of delivering reasonable returns. “We understand that investment requires certainty. That is what we strive to provide in Ghana. We know that projects must be bankable,” he said. He added that the government recognised the need for investments to be commercially sound and generate reasonable returns, assuring investors that Ghana was prepared to work with them to achieve those objectives. The Minister said investment partnerships must also respond to the expectations of Ghanaian citizens, particularly regarding employment, skills development, opportunities for local businesses and environmental protection. “Our citizens have equally legitimate expectations. They want jobs, skills, opportunities for local enterprise, protection of the environment, and a fair share of the prosperity produced from their own resources,” he said. Mr Buah maintained that these expectations could be reconciled with the need for successful businesses, stressing that responsible partnerships should deliver benefits to both investors and host countries. “Those expectations can be reconciled with the requirement of successful businesses,” he said. He noted that expectations of investment partnerships were changing across Africa as countries sought to strengthen their industries and institutions while deriving greater benefits from their natural resources. “Across Africa, our expectations of partnerships are changing,” he said. Mr Buah welcomed the contribution international partners could make through capital, technology, expertise and access to global markets, but stressed that these contributions should support Africa’s industrial development ambitions. “We welcome your capital, your technology, your experience, and your access to global markets. We ask and intend that you recognise our determination to build our industries and strengthen our institutions,” he said. He reiterated his invitation to investors to work with Ghana through fair negotiations, honouring commitments and establishing partnerships that deliver shared benefits. “The invitation is straightforward, Come and invest. Come and build with us. Let us negotiate fairly, honour our commitments, and work for outcomes that benefit both the investor and the host countries,” he said.

items.title: La Generalitat manda a la población de las comarcas de Gandia y Dénia que se confine en casa por las lluvias torrenciales e inundaciones
items.description: La dana Adam está castigando con extrema violencia e insistencia diversas poblaciones del norte de la provincia de Alicante, como Dénia y Pego, y del sur de Valencia, como Gandia. Una mujer de 79 años ha sido encontrada muerta este lunes en Oliva por efectivos de la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME). Un hombre también ha fallecido en un cámping de la localidad. El consejero valenciano de Emergencias, Juan Carlos Valderrama, ha pedido a los ciudadanos de estas poblaciones, integradas en las comarcas de La Safor y de La Marina Alta, que no salgan de casa y que no se desplacen ni circulen. “Por favor, confinamiento”, ha solicitado el consejero, tras la reunión del Cecopi (órgano de gestión de la emergencia), convocado esta mañana a las 7.00. La Generalitat ha publicado una orden en el Diari Oficial de la Comunitat Valenciana con la lista de 145 municipios cuyos vecinos, unos 850.000, deben quedarse en sus casas. Hay unas 2.000 personas evacuadas y se han llevado a cabo más de un centenar de rescates. Seguir leyendo

items.title: World will face a serious energy crisis if US launches another war against Iran
items.description: TEHRAN – More than seven months have passed since the United States, together with Israel, launched its war against Iran. What was meant to be a swift campaign to topple the Islamic Republic has instead left American bases across the region in ruins, the Strait of Hormuz still closed, and Washington without an answer to the energy crisis it helped create. With the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding in tatters and American midterm elections approaching, the question now is whether the US will risk another escalation — or accept defeat.

items.title: Passports: Nigerians in Qatar excited over improved service, honour Yakubu
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Nigerians in Qatar have honoured the Nigerian Ambassador to the country, Prof. Mahmood Yakubu, with an award for improved consular service, following the recent delivery of new passports to hundreds of them in a record time of two weeks. The presentation was made at an elaborate ceremony organised by the Nigerians in Diaspora Organisation NIDO, Qatar chapter, to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary. items.title: CAN de futsal 2026 : le Maroc défie l’Égypte pour une place en finale
items.description: Le Maroc affronte l’Égypte ce lundi 19 octobre à 20h, à Rabat, en demi-finale de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations de futsal 2026. Invaincus en phase de groupes et portés par une attaque particulièrement efficace, les Lions de l’Atlas, tenants du titre, devront se méfier de Pharaons déterminés à rejoindre la finale. Le dernier carré de la CAN de futsal 2026 promet une affiche de haut niveau. Le Maroc croise le fer avec l’Égypte ce lundi à 20h, dans la salle couverte du Complexe sportif Prince Moulay-Abdellah à Rabat. Une rencontre décisive pour les hommes de Hicham Dguig, qui ambitionnent de poursuivre leur parcours et de se rapprocher d’un nouveau sacre continental. À domicile, les Lions de l’Atlas abordent cette demi-finale avec confiance, après avoir réalisé un premier tour parfait. Ils ont remporté leurs trois rencontres de groupe face à l’Algérie (4-0), à la Zambie (7-0) et à la Libye (6-0). Avec 17 buts inscrits et aucun encaissé, la sélection marocaine a affiché une remarquable efficacité offensive, tout en confirmant sa solidité défensive. Ce bilan place le Maroc parmi les grands favoris de la compétition. Mais face à l’Égypte, l’opposition s’annonce plus exigeante. Les demi-finales ne laissent que peu de place à l’erreur et imposent une concentration constante, notamment face à une équipe expérimentée sur la scène continentale. L’Égypte veut créer la surprise Les Pharaons ont terminé deuxièmes du groupe B avec six points. Ils ont débuté leur parcours par deux larges victoires contre la Tanzanie (8-0) et le Mozambique (4-0), avant de s’incliner face à l’Angola (2-4) lors de leur dernier match de groupe. Malgré ce revers, la sélection égyptienne conserve des arguments pour rivaliser avec le Maroc. Son expérience des grandes compétitions et ses capacités offensives pourraient lui permettre de poser des difficultés aux champions en titre. Pour espérer se qualifier, les Égyptiens devront notamment se montrer plus rigoureux dans leur organisation défensive et limiter les espaces laissés aux joueurs marocains. Ils devront également mieux gérer les temps forts des Lions de l’Atlas, qui ont démontré leur capacité à multiplier les occasions et à concrétiser leur domination. De son côté, le Maroc devra rester vigilant dans les transitions et éviter toute précipitation. La maîtrise du rythme et l’efficacité devant le but pourraient peser lourd dans cette confrontation. Hicham Dguig vise une nouvelle finale Pour le sélectionneur Hicham Dguig et ses joueurs, l’objectif est clair : poursuivre sur la lancée de la phase de groupes et décrocher une place en finale. La solidité défensive affichée depuis le début du tournoi constitue un atout important, mais le staff devra également préparer son équipe à une opposition susceptible de se montrer plus agressive et plus disciplinée tactiquement. Le soutien du public marocain pourrait également jouer un rôle dans cette rencontre disputée à Rabat. Face à des Pharaons désireux de rebondir après leur défaite contre l’Angola, les Lions devront néanmoins faire preuve de maîtrise et de lucidité dans les moments décisifs. Cette demi-finale représente ainsi un test important pour les champions en titre. Une victoire leur ouvrirait les portes de la finale et les rapprocherait d’un nouveau trophée continental. Mais avant de penser au sacre, les hommes de Hicham Dguig devront franchir l’obstacle égyptien dans un duel qui s’annonce particulièrement disputé. The post CAN de futsal 2026 : le Maroc défie l’Égypte pour une place en finale appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Un appel à la générosité citoyenne pour doter la commune Agoè-Nyivé 5 d’engins de travaux publics
items.description: Agoè-Nyivé, 19 oct. (ATOP) – Le maire de la commune Agoè-Nyivé 5, Lamadokou Kossi, a lancé officiellement le projet « Appel à la générosité citoyenne », le samedi 17 octobre à Sanguéra, chef-lieu de la commune. Cette initiative vise à mobiliser 400 millions de FCFA sur cinq ans pour acquérir des engins de travaux publics destinés à améliorer l’état des voies et à faciliter la mobilité des populations. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence du préfet d’Agoè-Nyivé, Dr Tinaka Wédiabalo Kossi, du secrétaire général de la commune d’Agoè-Nyivé 5, des conseillers municipaux, du chef de canton, des chefs village, des responsables communautaires et des membres des Comités villageois de développement (CVD). L’assistance Au cours de la rencontre, le président du comité de mobilisation des ressources, Atantsi Edem, a indiqué que le projet permettra l’acquisition de sept engins stratégiques, à savoir un grader, deux camions-bennes, un compacteur, une chargeuse, une pelle hydraulique et un bulldozer. « Ces équipements permettront d’aménager et de stabiliser les voies d’accès dans la commune, contribuant ainsi à améliorer les conditions de déplacement des populations et à faciliter leurs activités quotidiennes », a ajouté le président du comité. M. Atantsi a également présenté les différents moyens prévus pour effectuer les dons, notamment les transferts par mobile money, le virement postal et les contributions en espèces. Les dons remis en main propre donneront lieu à la délivrance immédiate d’un reçu. Le maire d’Agoè-Nyivé 5, Lamadokou Kossi, a souligné que la réussite de cette initiative repose sur la bonne volonté et la mobilisation de tous les citoyens. Il a rappelé l’importance des voies dans la vie quotidienne des habitants. Le maire a annoncé que les premiers engins devraient être acquis dans les six prochains mois, tandis que les autres équipements seront achetés progressivement, en fonction de l’évolution de la mobilisation des ressources. À travers cet appel à la générosité citoyenne, la commune Agoè-Nyivé 5 entend renforcer les moyens matériels nécessaires à l’entretien et à l’aménagement de son réseau routier. ATOP/ASA/AR

items.title: Lebanon’s ‘pilot zone’ experiment: The case of Zawtar al-Gharbiyah
items.description: Ihsan Yaghi’s house in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah is scorched from the inside. Piles of rubble fill the rooms she and her husband walk through to see what remains. What was not demolished by nearby Israeli strikes has been blackened by fire, with soot covering the interior walls. But Yaghi refuses to leave. “Despite everything, this is still my land, and we have a very strong attachment to this land that we can’t let go of,” Yaghi tells Mada Masr. Yaghi’s is one of roughly 100 families that have, since July, returned to Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, one of around 70 villages in southern Lebanon still under Israeli occupation, its residents displaced, its homes destroyed, its fields unreachable. The question of what should be done for the south, how to rebuild and how to return people to their land under continued occupation, has become one of the most pressing political questions in Lebanon. The answer currently on offer from the Lebanese government and its international partners is the “pilot zone.” On July 21, the United States announced the official commencement of pilot zone operations in three villages in southern Lebanon: Froun, Srifa and Zawtar al-Gharbiyah. The model emerged from the framework agreement — a US-mediated trilateral framework signed by Lebanon and Israel on June 26, under which the Lebanese military is to restore sovereign authority over all Lebanese territory pending Hezbollah’s disarmament. The implementation of pilot zones was to mark the agreement’s first practical step. The idea was that the Lebanese military would deploy to select villages in coordination with a limited Israeli withdrawal, allowing residents to return while reconstruction and services would be concentrated there. Those villages would serve as templates, proof that return and rebuilding are possible, and the model could then be replicated elsewhere in the south. Mada Masr spoke to residents, municipal officials and others involved with the project to assess whether this is indeed a workable model for the south. Two months in, it is falling short on nearly every measure residents say matters. People are returning to villages without water, electricity, schools or livelihoods, the prefabricated homes promised as a temporary fix have arrived at a fraction of the numbers requested, and there is no guarantee of safety so long as Israeli forces remain in position nearby and have not withdrawn. Children walking by destroyed houses in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, July 26. Photo by Ammar Ammar. The model also treats villages as isolated units, when in reality they depend on one another for schools, shops, hospitals and work, activists say. While experts on the South’s history of war and reconstruction say the current process marks a fundamental shift from previous rounds of war, for those in the south adopting a more radical position on resistance, another pathway must be found. *** The pilot zone is a new model for the south. Political historian Nassib Chams tells Mada Masr that it emerged from a major shift in Lebanese politics: direct talks with Israel. Such talks were not the case during the 2000 Israeli withdrawal, after 20 years of occupation, or after the 2006 war. That shift, he says, is what allowed the pilot zone project to come into being, and it gives Israel agency and authority over the return of southern Lebanese. “This is the first time in Lebanese history that we see many Lebanese expressing that they want peace with Israel. So, while Israel was always stronger militarily, it is the first time there is this much political support for Israel,” he notes. He adds that the project remains loosely defined, with the government yet to give residents a clear account of what the pilot zones entail. “We may not know what is in it. We don’t know the details of what is happening in the negotiations. So far, we have not seen an Israeli withdrawal or anything. Israeli military operations are still continuing,” he says. “Are the people supposed to test if their villages are still habitable? It is unclear what they are trying to achieve when it is not even contingent on a full Israeli withdrawal,” he says. Israeli forces in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, September 24. Photo by Ammar Ammar. A resident of Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, speaking on condition of anonymity, tells Mada Masr that Froun and Srifa have no Israeli presence at all, while Zawtar al-Gharbiyah has a relatively limited presence of Israeli troops compared to its twin village, Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, which remains under occupation and continues to face airstrikes, artillery shelling and the demolition of homes. The two villages sit in the Nabatieh District, on elevated terrain north of the Litani River, overlooking its valley, with Zawtar al-Sharqiyah immediately to the east of Zawtar al-Gharbiyah and with Mayfadoun to their north and Qaaqaaiyet al-Jisr to the west. Following the July 21 announcement, the Lebanese military deployed to Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, and residents were allowed to return. What they found was widespread destruction of residential buildings, infrastructure, schools, supermarkets, hospitals and government offices. To the west of the village, Israeli forces remain positioned behind an earthen berm, blocking access to the rest of the village. Earthen beam Israeli forces placed between Zawtar al-Gharbiyah and Zawtar al-Sharqiyah. Photo by Ammar Ammar. Israeli forces are now 300-400 metres away, according to Yaghi. The Lebanese military has set up a checkpoint some 20 metres from the berm, which gives residents a sense of security and protection, she adds. “The thing that encouraged people to return is the presence of the Lebanese military,” Abed Ezz Eddin, Zawtar al-Gharbiyah’s mayor, tells Mada Masr. “People feel safe knowing that the Lebanese military is present among us,” he says. Lebanese military assisting residents’ return to Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, July 24. Photo by Ammar Ammar. *** Two months into the start of the pilot zones, only 16 out of 263 requested prefabricated homes have reached Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, according to Ezz Eddin. The units were secured through a joint project between the Council of the South, a governmental institution tasked with providing assistance and compensation to the people affected by war and disasters in southern Lebanon, and the government’s High Relief Committee (HRC). Bassam Naboulsy, the high committee’s director, tells Mada Masr that the government tasked the committee with securing 150 units, sourced through a mix of locally purchased units funded by the HRC and units brought in from East Asia by a private Swiss organization, whose name Naboulsy did not disclose. “These houses will be distributed between Zawtar al-Gharbiyah and nearby villages, such as Merouaniyeh and Froun,” he says. Naboulsy adds that the distribution process is being handled by the southern council and local municipalities. Prefabricated homes can cost around US$5,000 per unit, according to Naboulsy, a figure that he says exceeds the government’s limited budget and has thus necessitated having to rely on foreign assistance. As a result, there are no guarantees on how many units will arrive or when. In late July, Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan , who agreed to provide prefabricated homes to Lebanon, with no guaranteed timeline. Even when the units arrive, they need to be made ready. Ezz Eddin says the land beneath them must first be cleared of debris and prepared before the winter rains, a process overseen by the Council of the South. The units also need solar panels, water tanks and kitchen appliances, for which Zawtar al-Gharbiyah’s municipality is seeking support from nongovernmental organizations. A prefabricated home in place of a destroyed house, October 14. Photo by Ammar Ammar. Much of the work of return has fallen on the municipality and on residents themselves. Ezz Eddin says the municipality has been left to restore power lines, work on water infrastructure and seek foreign funding for both. “People are paying out of pocket to fix their houses to be able to stay in them,” he says. “But even then, people are hesitant to put glass in their windows and are just using plastic wrap instead.” For those who have returned, making a living remains difficult. Zawtar relies on agriculture, but venturing into fields, particularly those farther from the village center, has become risky. Residents need permission from the Mechanism , a committee comprising Lebanon, Israel, France and UNIFIL tasked with overseeing the ceasefire. The Lebanese military communicates residents’ requests to the Mechanism, Ezz Eddin says, but so far, they have not received permission to access their fields. “Even if I wanted to plant my own field around the house, I need to remove the debris on my own. So my husband and I are having to rent a bulldozer to do that ourselves,” Yaghi says. She currently comes to the village only during the day and leaves for a nearby village at night, as her house remains unrepaired and unlivable. *** The limits of the pilot zones are already clear in villages it has yet to reach. Tarek Mazraany, an activist and the founder of grassroots initiative the Gathering of the Children of the Southern Border Towns, says the model would be difficult to replicate because it treats each village separately and overlooks how much residents depend on neighboring villages for schools, shops, hospitals and work. “Zawtar al-Gharbiyah is a relatively small village, and it took two months to start securing prefabricated houses,” Mazraany says. “This can’t be sustainable in other villages, particularly those near the border, where the scale of destruction is much greater and many have become totally isolated,” he adds. Zawtar al-Gharbiyah also has an advantage because of its proximity to Nabatieh, which gives residents access to shops, schools and government offices. In villages closer to the border, where destruction is far more extensive, clearing the rubble alone could take years. Rebuilding homes will not be enough, Mazraany says. Residents also need schools, shops, hospitals and law enforcement services to return before they can fully resume their lives. He argues that reconstruction should instead be organized by district, with neighboring villages rebuilt together so they can share services and speed up residents’ return. “The best model would be to work district by district as pilot zones, because villages in the broader South depend on each other. One can have the school, the other can have the shops, so that the process is quicker and more residents can return,” he says. Reconstruction in some of the larger towns, such as Bint Jbeil and Khiam, could take up to 20 years, Mazraany says, adding that time is not on southern residents’ side if the government continues to delay their return. *** While those Mada Masr spoke to see the pilot zones as a failed approach to reconstruction, those committed to a more radical position on resistance reject the project altogether, refusing to recognize the agreement on which it is based. “We consider all the land to be our land, and it is our right to be in any place in southern Lebanon and in any village in southern Lebanon, regardless of whether the enemy withdrew under conditions or without conditions,” Afif Shuman, the director of NGO Wa Taawano, tells Mada Masr. “We do not turn to and we are not ready even to coordinate with the Mechanism or any party that may be coordinating with the Israelis.” Wa Taawano is one of the most active charities in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah. But Shuman says the security situation, particularly the constant presence of Israeli drones overhead, has made it difficult for activists and NGOs to operate safely. Shuman also points to political and security pressures that he says are preventing aid from reaching southern residents. He says some charities affiliated with Lebanese political figures withheld assistance to appease the US, while others refrained from operating in areas affected by the fighting for fear of security repercussions and possible sanctions. For Shuman, the pilot zones are not a reconstruction model but a way to determine who is allowed to return. He argues that the project is designed to exclude families Israel does not want back in their villages, including the families of those killed in the fighting and the fighters themselves. He says residents would not accept a system that prevents them from returning to their homes, making the project unworkable in the long run. Hajj Ali Khazaal, the head of the municipality in Ainata, a border village in the Bint Jbeil district, and the head of Hezbollah’s municipality affairs for the south, holds a similar position. “I do not fundamentally recognize the framework agreement that this project came out of,” Khazaal tells Mada Masr. Khazaal says the Lebanese military’s deployment to all southern villages should be the government’s main priority, which would require a complete Israeli withdrawal. He describes the pressure on the region as military, political and financial, arguing that the state has also failed residents by leaving reconstruction unaddressed. “They want reconstruction without resistance so that they can get rid of the resistance, but that will be futile. There should be a clear focus on reconstruction and people’s immediate return,” he says. Khazaal also pointed to US President Donald Trump’s proposal for an economic zone spanning more than two dozen towns in southern Lebanon, focused on development and investment — not the Lebanese people’s return — as more likely to move forward than the pilot zones. For Khazaal, the first step before reconstruction can begin must be to secure the withdrawal of Israeli forces and regain access to all the land. He says the municipality already has a plan for the process, which he estimates would take around three years. Clearing rubble would take six months to a year, followed by another six to 12 months to reopen roads and restore water and electricity infrastructure. Installing prefabricated homes and making them habitable would then take another year to a year and a half. In the meantime, he argues, negotiations are wasting time while the decisions shaping southern Lebanon’s future are being made elsewhere. “The Iranian-American agreement, wherever things go there is reflected here,” he says. “All of this is a waste of time here, until the decision comes from those superior.” Lebanon and Israel are expected to hold a new round of negotiations in Florida, around the end of October, where the possibility of a second pilot zone could be discussed. And while the US and Israel have tried to push forward their plans for the south, Hezbollah and Iran have not remained confined to criticism. Hezbollah’s Executive Council head Ali Damoush addresses a press conference in southern Beirut, October 13. Courtesy of Anwar Amro/AFP On October 13, Hezbollah announced it would begin paying rent compensation to people whose homes were destroyed, with payments reaching as much as $14,000 for housing units in Beirut and its southern suburbs and $12,000 elsewhere, starting with an initial installment of $3,500 in Beirut and its southern suburbs and $3,000 outside those areas. The announcement of the cash payouts come after Iran transferred $600 million to Hezbollah at the beginning of October via Syrian intermediaries, an Iranian diplomat, a Syrian source with direct knowledge of the transfer and a source in the party tell Mada Masr. The money, the Iranian diplomat says, aims to help the displaced ahead of the coming winter. For families like Yaghi’s, promises for support from either side are still yet to materialize, and, for now, there is nothing to do apart from carrying on. “Seeing how attached our neighbors are to the land,” she says, “and how adamant they are to remain present, gives us the strength to stay and endure.” The post Lebanon’s ‘pilot zone’ experiment: The case of Zawtar al-Gharbiyah first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Cap-Skirring : les hôteliers réclament la réfection de la route Ziguinchor-Cap et des vols réguliers
items.description: À l’ouverture de la saison touristique 2026-2027, le Collectif des acteurs économiques et touristiques de la Casamance plaide pour la réhabilitation de la route reliant Ziguinchor à Cap-Skirring et la programmation de vols réguliers, afin de faciliter l’accès à cette destination balnéaire du sud du Sénégal. La qualité de la route entre Ziguinchor et Cap-Skirring et l’irrégularité des dessertes aériennes préoccupent les acteurs du tourisme en Casamance. Le Collectif des acteurs économiques et touristiques de la Casamance, d'après l'APS, réclame des infrastructures routières adaptées et une meilleure régularité des vols pour renforcer l’attractivité de la destination. « Pour venir à Cap-Skirring, une distance de 70 km, vous pouvez faire plus de deux heures de temps, à cause de la route, qui est d’une très mauvaise qualité », a déclaré dimanche Doudou Tamba, président du collectif, lors d’une conférence de presse. Selon lui, les difficultés d’accès à la station balnéaire constituent un obstacle au développement du tourisme. Cette situation peut notamment inciter certains visiteurs à prolonger leur séjour à Ziguinchor plutôt que de poursuivre leur déplacement vers Cap-Skirring. Les professionnels du secteur plaident également pour la programmation de vols réguliers, notamment par des compagnies comme Air Sénégal. Ils estiment que les annulations de vols enregistrées l’année dernière ont entraîné des pertes de clients et fragilisé l’activité touristique. Doudou Tamba considère que les incertitudes liées aux dessertes aériennes, entre retards, imprévus et annulations, constituent « un frein majeur » à la promotion de la destination. « Cette année, la saison a bien commencé. La Casamance attire toujours autant de monde. Les gens qui viennent ont envie de rester, mais le secteur doit être soutenu par des infrastructures et des services fiables », a-t-il souligné. La saison touristique 2026-2027 a été lancée dimanche en Casamance et doit s’étendre sur plus de sept mois. Un premier vol affrété par le Club Med, transportant 175 passagers en provenance de France, a déjà atterri à l’aéroport international de Cap-Skirring. Pour accompagner ce démarrage, le collectif des hôteliers opérant dans la station balnéaire prévoit une semaine culturelle, qui sera clôturée par un grand concert de l’artiste Omar Pène, lead vocal du Super Diamono. Avant ce rendez-vous, le chanteur doit effectuer des visites dans plusieurs villages de Casamance. À travers leurs revendications, les acteurs économiques et touristiques entendent attirer l’attention sur les conditions d’accès à Cap-Skirring et la nécessité de disposer de moyens de transport fiables pour soutenir durablement l’activité touristique dans la région.

items.title: Marseille’s official store looted as protests rock France
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Olympique de Marseille’s official store on the city’s La Canebière avenue was looted during weekend unrest, the Ligue 1 club said on Monday. According to Reuters, the incident came as France experienced some of its worst unrest in years, with protests over rising prices and declining public services. Thousands of people were arrested, while shops were looted or damaged. Marseille authorities imposed a ban on public gatherings and demonstrations across the city on Monday following violent protests and looting. The club condemned the attack and said it stood in solidarity with Puma, its partner that operates the store. The damage has forced the shop to close temporarily, though fans can still visit Marseille’s other official stores. Marseille said it would update supporters when conditions allow the La Canebière store to reopen. The club said in a statement: “Olympique de Marseille condemns in the strongest possible terms the acts of violence and looting targeting its official store on the Canebière and expresses its solidarity with its partner Puma, which operates the store. These events have caused significant property damage, forcing the club to temporarily close this store to the public. Fans may, however, continue to visit OM’s other official stores in Marseille. The club will inform its fans as soon as conditions allow for a reopening.” The club sits ninth in Ligue 1 after seven matches. It returns to action on Thursday with an away Europa League game against Austria’s Sturm Graz. The post Marseille’s official store looted as protests rock France appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Former Delta governor Uduaghan dies at 71
items.description: By Akpokona Omafuaire Former Governor of Delta State Emmanuel Uduaghan has died just three days before his 72nd birthday, according to his family. A statement signed by his son Toju Anire Uduaghan on behalf of the family said the ex-governor died on Monday. Read Also: Uduaghan is alive, recuperating – Family, aide debunk death rumour “It is with hearts weighed down by immeasurable grief and profound sorrow that we announce the passing to glory of our beloved Father, Brother, Uncle, and Patriarch, His Excellency, Dr. Chief Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, former Governor of Delta State, who departed this world on the morning of 19th October 2026,” the statement said. “His passing has left us devastated. Words can hardly express the depth of our sorrow at the loss of a man who meant so much to our family and whose life and service touched countless others across Delta State and Nigeria. “He was a source of strength, a father figure, a beloved brother and uncle, and a respected elder. We will deeply miss his presence and forever cherish the memories and legacy he leaves behind. “He served as Commissioner for Health from 1999 to 2003, Secretary to the Delta State Government from 2003 to 2007, and Governor of Delta State from 2007 to 2015. Throughout his years in public service, he demonstrated a commitment to the human and infrastructural development of Delta State.” The statement said Uduaghan’s death was a profound loss to the family, the people of Delta State, and Nigeria at large. “We are grateful to Almighty God for his life, his service, and the legacy he leaves behind. “We pray that Almighty God, in His infinite mercy, will grant his soul eternal rest and comfort our family, friends, associates, former colleagues, and all who mourn this painful loss,” the statement added. Vanguard News The post Former Delta governor Uduaghan dies at 71 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Musk and Anthropic pledge public share giveaways
items.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX and artificial intelligence giant Anthropic have pledged big financial giveaways as Big Tech firms come under pressure over the potential impact of AI on humanity. Musk said on Monday that he would give one of his shares at his rocket company, which owns xAI, to every child in America next year. The billionaire’s announcement came after Anthropic said it would commit 5% of its shares to a fund that will make donations for the “public good”. Anthropic is laying the ground for a potential blockbuster stock market listing that could value the firm at more than $1tn (£750bn). SpaceX set the record for biggest initial public offering (IPO) in history in June, raising $85.7bn. The pledges come at a time when the AI industry is under intense scrutiny over safety concerns and fears about its impact on society and jobs. Details over how each American child would be handed a share in SpaceX have not been disclosed. In a post on social media, Musk said: “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many.” It came after he responded to Anthropic’s public fund pledge with: “I recommend giving the shares directly to the public. This is what I will be doing.” Anthropic said none of the shares held in its Public Benefit Fund would be used for lobbying or political donations in the US or overseas. The Claude developer said on Sunday that the fund could also receive another 2% of the firm’s shares at its board’s discretion. Last week, Anthropic told prospective investors that its revenue surged by 45% to $16.8bn (£12.6bn) in the three months to the end of September. In common with other AI firms, it is seeking to position itself as being able to generate huge profits despite spending billions on developing the technology and building infrastructure to power its models. Companies around the world, primarily technology firms, have cut thousands of jobs after investing in AI, with many pointing to higher efficiencies from its adoption. Research by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) published in 2024 suggested that almost 40% of jobs around the world will be affected by AI, with that figure rising as high as ​60% in advanced economies. In September, a researcher who quit Anthropic said people working on the technology were “genuinely frightened” about the speed of its advancements and what it could mean for humanity. “I believe that if we don’t slow down at the current rate of progress, there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future,” he said. Jacob Coxon was speaking to the BBC after his resignation post on the dangers of AI went viral on a backdrop of growing safety concerns about the industry. The 27-year-old’s former boss, Anthropic head Dario Amodei, had previously called for AI development to slow down – though some have questioned the motivations behind this. The bosses of two rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Musk, have both said they agree with Amodei’s proposal for industry-wide deceleration and regulation, as well as independent monitoring of AI model development. Earlier this month, US President Donald Trump and the heads of major AI firms signed a “morally binding” document, making them responsible for ensuring the safety of their own technology. Trump has repeatedly rejected the idea of laws to control development of the technology despite a debate about the potential risks of AI and what it means for humanity. Since then, the president has named the director of national intelligence Jay Clayton as the head of a new taskforce on AI which, he said, will co-ordinate government engagement with consumers, companies and “religious organizations”.

Kwadaso Assembly plants 400 royal palms to promote green environment
items.description: The Kwadaso Municipal Assembly has embarked on a large-scale tree planting exercise at Diamond Valley, a sub-community of Denkyemuoso, as part of its efforts to mitigate the effects of climate change and promote a green environment. The exercise, which was led by the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE), Eric Asibey, saw the planting of about 400 royal palm trees along principal streets, frontages of houses, and identified open spaces within the fast-developing residential enclave. The MCE explained the project goes beyond beautification, as it is a strategic intervention to reduce carbon emissions, improve air quality, control erosion, and provide shade. He noted that urban communities like Diamond Valley are increasingly experiencing the adverse effects of climate change, including excessive heat and poor air circulation, which can be addressed through deliberate tree planting. “Planting these royal palm trees will not only help fight climate change but will also enhance the beauty of this community and make Kwadaso a model green municipality. Trees are life, and we must consciously protect our environment for future generations,” he stated. Mr. Asibey commended the residents for their cooperation and assured them that the Assembly will continue to roll out similar greening interventions across other communities within the municipality. The MCE further acknowledged the major concern of residents regarding the poor condition of roads in the area. He noted that most residents are prominent individuals who are able to provide for themselves basic amenities such as water and streetlights, but road infrastructure remains their biggest challenge. He assured the residents of his commitment to lobby for the construction of the roads to ease movement and improve living conditions. “The state of the roads here is deplorable and I understand your concerns. I will do everything within my power to ensure these roads are constructed for your convenience,” Mr. Asibey assured. Chairman of the Diamond Valley Residents Association, Dr. Emmanuel Ati, commended the Assembly for the initiative and charged members of the association to take ownership of the project to ensure its sustainability. He urged residents to nurture the trees planted in front of their homes and promised that the association would replace any seedlings that fail to survive. “We must all take good care of these trees. It is our responsibility to water them and ensure they grow. The association will monitor and replace any seedlings that fail to survive, but we need the commitment of every household,” Dr. Ati emphasised. Some residents who took part in the exercise also commended the Assembly for the initiative, describing it as timely, and pledged their full support to maintain the trees to ensure the sustainability of the project. The exercise was carried out in collaboration with the Diamond Valley Residents Association and forms part of ongoing efforts by the Kwadaso Municipal Assembly to promote environmental sustainability in the municipality.

items.title: Gov’t seizes 8,200 items in galamsey fight, including 135 excavators – Mahama
items.description: President John Mahama says his government has confiscated 8,200 items used in illegal mining, commonly known as galamsey, across the country. Speaking at the Mining in Motion conference on Monday, 19th October, he said the seized items included 135 excavators and more than 200 firearms. “We have achieved some successes in the fight against illegal mining. We have confiscated more than 8,200 items, this includes Chan-fan machines, excavators and other equipment use in illegal mining,” “We have confiscated 135 excavators that were used in illegal mining, and we have retrieved almost 200 firearms that people involved in illegal mining have,” the president revealed at the conference held in Accra to discuss the country’s extractive sector. The figures outline the scale of equipment and weapons recovered through the government’s efforts to tackle illegal mining, the president noted and commended those working in the area. “I commend the efforts of all those involved in the fight against illegal mining and those involved in the fight against environmental destruction,” the president said. Illegal mining remains a major concern in Ghana because of its impact on water bodies, forests and agricultural land.

items.title: Tension over alleged bloated voters’ register at Atwima Kwanwoma NDC ahead of constituency elections
items.description: Tension is mounting within the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Atwima Kwanwoma Constituency of the Ashanti Region, following concerns raised by the party’s women’s wing over an alleged bloated voters’ register ahead of Saturday’s constituency elections. The women are calling on the party’s regional and national executives to urgently intervene in the matter to prevent further escalation of tensions ahead of the polls. Addressing a press conference, the Atwima Kwanwoma NDC Women Organiser, Afia Serwaa, alleged that the names of several women and other longstanding party members had been removed from the party’s register, a development she said was creating confusion and mistrust among members. She claimed that more than 700 party members had been removed from the register and replaced with names of individuals she described as non-party members. “Over 700 party members, including women, have had their names removed and replaced with those of non-party members. In some instances, a woman’s name appears alongside a man’s photograph and telephone number. We suspect this is a deliberate attempt by some individuals to manipulate the elections in their favour,” she alleged. Ms. Serwaa further claimed that the matter had been reported to the party’s regional executives on several occasions, but no action had been taken to address their concerns. She therefore appealed to the national executives to intervene before Saturday’s elections, warning that the alleged irregularities could undermine the party’s unity in the constituency. According to her, the conduct of some party executives was gradually eroding confidence in the party’s internal structures in Atwima Kwanwoma. Some aspirants who also spoke to the media expressed frustration over the alleged irregularities, warning that failure to resolve the concerns before the elections could trigger further unrest within the constituency. They accused some individuals of seeking to use their personal interests to influence the party’s internal electoral process. Some of the women who attended the press conference also threatened to stage a naked demonstration if their names were not restored to the party’s register before the elections. They alleged that some aspirants were attempting to manipulate the electoral process to secure victory for their personal interests. The concerns come ahead of Saturday’s constituency elections, with the aggrieved members urging the party’s leadership to urgently investigate the allegations and ensure a credible, transparent and peaceful electoral process.

items.title: GFA labels Björkegren ‘best-performing coach’ to justify Black Stars appointment
items.description: The Ghana Football Association (GFA) has defended the appointment of Kim Lars Björkegren as interim Black Stars coach, describing him as the “best-performing coach” among the country’s various national teams. The Swedish coach, who is in charge of the Black Queens, has been handed the men’s senior national team role on a temporary basis for the upcoming Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Somalia. A five-member committee recommended Björkegren for the position, with Ibrahim Tanko and Godwin Attram serving as his assistants, following Carlos Queiroz’s departure from the GFA. “The committee looked within and settled on Kim Lars Björkegren because he is the best-performing coach in terms of the national teams, so I don’t think it will be a challenge for him,” GFA Communications Director Henry Asante Twum told Asempa FM. “The committee felt we have to look at someone who worked with Carlos Queiroz, and it is obviously Godwin Attram,” he said. “Ibrahim Tanko is the best coach in the country at the moment. He is the defending champion of the Ghana Premier League and currently sits at the top of the league,” he added. Meanwhile, the Black Queens are set to face Ecuador, Uzbekistan and Papua New Guinea in the World Cup play-off tournament, which is reportedly scheduled to take place in Morocco on November 28, 13 days after Ghana’s second qualifier against Somalia. Asked whether Björkegren’s appointment could affect the Black Queens’ preparations for the play-offs, Asante Twum said: “We are aware that the Black Queens will prepare next month for the World Cup play-offs, but I don’t think that his appointment will be a hindrance.”

items.title: Abascal reitera su oferta de acuerdo al PP para “proteger al Senado” del pacto de izquierdas
items.description: El líder de Vox, Santiago Abascal, ha reiterado su oferta de llegar “a algún entendimiento [con el PP] para proteger al Senado del pacto de Sánchez con la extrema izquierda”; en alusión a la candidatura conjunta Senado de Progreso , que el PSOE y el Frente Amplio presentarán en 45 circunscripciones en las elecciones del 29 de noviembre. Aunque ha expresado su disposición a realizar “sacrificios”, no ha detallado en qué consistirá el pacto: si Vox no se presentará en las provincias en las que no tiene ninguna posibilidad de sacar escaño (en las elecciones de 2023 no obtuvo ni un senador en las urnas) o presentará solo un candidato por circunscripción (cada partido presenta un máximo de tres candidatos al Senado, pero los elegidos son cuatro por provincia). El líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, también podría compensar a Abascal con senadores autonómicos, hasta lograr los diez requeridos para formar grupo parlamentario en la Cámara alta. De hecho, los cuatro senadores que tiene ahora Vox fueron elegidos por las asambleas de Extremadura, Aragón y Andalucía. Se tratará, en todo caso, del primer acuerdo preelectoral que alcanzan PP y Vox. Para cerrarlo aún disponen de una semana, pues el plazo para presentar las candidaturas acaba el día 26. items.title: Vista Bank Burkina: Moumounou Gnankambary nommé nouveau directeur général
items.description: L’expert burkinabè en gouvernance financière, Moumounou Gnankambary, a été nommé nouveau directeur général de Vista Bank Burkina, en remplacement de Mohamed Ba, à l’issue d’une réunion à Bangkok, le vendredi 16 octobre 2026. L’ancien Conseiller technique du ministère burkinabè de l’Economie et des Finances, Moumounou Gnankambary, a été nommé au poste de directeur général, le vendredi 16 octobre 2026, à l’issue d’une réunion qui a rassemblée les premiers responsables du Groupe Vista à Bangkok en Thaïlande. Selon certains médias, M. Gnankambary aura la charge de poursuivre la fusion de la banque avec la Société Générale Burkina Faso (SGBF), ancienne banque française, qu’avait commencé l’ancien directeur général Mohamed Ba. La désignation de Moumounou Gnankambary à la tête de Vista Bank Burkina marque une étape déterminante dans la restructuration du marché bancaire burkinabè. Conseiller Technique du ministre de l'Economie et des Finances d'octobre 2015 à avril 2021, Moumounou Gnankambary a été également le directeur général du Trésor et de la Comptabilité publique d'août 2007 à janvier 2015. Il a été aussi directeur général du Budget de février 2005 à juillet 2007 et Directeur administratif et financier (DAF) de la Présidence du Faso de janvier 2000 à janvier 2005. Par Wakat Séra L’article Vista Bank Burkina: Moumounou Gnankambary nommé nouveau directeur général est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Court of Appeal halts former NAFCO boss’s trial over charge sheet challenge
items.description: The Court of Appeal has halted the trial of former Chief Executive Officer of the National Food and Buffer Stock Company (NAFCO), Hanan Abdul-Wahab Aludiba, pending the determination of his appeal challenging the charge sheet. A three-member panel, presided over by Justice Noble Nkrumah, granted the stay of proceedings on Monday, October 19, 2026, after finding that the issues raised by his lawyers constituted exceptional circumstances. The panel, which also included Justices Lydia Osei Marfo and George Boadi, heard arguments from lawyers for Hanan and the Republic before granting the application. Hanan is appealing a July 2026 High Court ruling that dismissed his application to quash the charges on grounds of alleged defects in the charge sheet. The charges against him and his wife, Faiza Seidu Wuni, include stealing, defrauding by false pretences, wilfully causing financial loss to the Republic, using public office for profit, dishonestly receiving, money laundering and intentional misapplication of public funds. Arguing for the suspension of the trial, his lead counsel, former Attorney-General Godfred Yeboah Dame, said the alleged defects raised fundamental questions about his client’s right to a fair trial. He argued that proceeding before the appeal was determined could result in a substantial miscarriage of justice, as the charge sheet must provide sufficient particulars to enable an accused person to understand the allegations and prepare a defence. Mr Dame challenged counts three, 13 and 18, which concern stealing, arguing that the prosecution had grouped several transactions into individual counts without adequately identifying the alleged acts. He cited count three, which alleges that Hanan stole GH¢50 million through payments made between 2017 and 2025. He argued that the period was too broad and that the charge did not identify the individual transactions underlying the allegation. According to Mr Dame, although the prosecution’s statement of facts referred to 86 transactions, those details were absent from the charge sheet. He further argued that the prosecution had not explained how the alleged stealing occurred beyond describing the offence as “stealing”. Relying on Section 109 of the Criminal and Other Offences (Procedure) Act, 1960 (Act 30), Mr Dame submitted that distinct acts constituting separate offences should be charged separately. On the allegation of defrauding by false pretences, he argued that count one did not identify the alleged false representation through which the money was obtained. He also told the court that the appeal could be heard without undue delay because the record of appeal was ready. Opposing the application, Deputy Attorney-General Dr Justice Srem-Sai argued that Hanan had failed to establish exceptional circumstances to justify suspending the trial. He said disagreement with a trial court’s ruling was not sufficient grounds for a stay of proceedings. Dr Srem-Sai maintained that the charge sheet adequately informed the accused persons of the allegations against them. He also argued that offences committed repeatedly over a period could be grouped in a charge and that the law required particulars to be stated in ordinary language rather than technical terms. He warned that halting the trial could cause unnecessary delays, particularly if the appeal failed. In response, Mr Dame maintained that the accused persons were entitled to challenge the charge sheet. He also disputed the prosecution’s argument about repeated offences, saying it was not supported by the particulars provided. Delivering its ruling, the panel said the charge sheet formed the foundation of the trial. “Having listened, we take the position that the charge sheet carries the superstructure of the trial,” the court said. It held that the issues raised warranted a stay and suspended the High Court proceedings pending the determination of the appeal. The ruling does not determine the merits of the charges or resolve the challenge to the charge sheet.

items.title: Mining must benefit communities without destroying their environment – Lands Minister
items.description: Lands and Natural Resources Minister Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah has described responsible mining as a key measure of Ghana’s progress, stressing that mineral extraction must benefit local communities without leaving them to bear the environmental and social costs. In an address at the 2026 Mining in Motion Conference on Monday, October 19, under the theme ‘One Continent, One Voice on Minerals: Aligning Africa’s Minerals Future’, Mr Buah said communities living closest to mineral resources must be able to experience the benefits of mining while their lands and water bodies are protected from environmental damage. “On responsible mining, there is another test for our progress. The people who live closest to mineral wealth should be able to recognise its benefits, and their rivers and lands should not be left to carry its costs,” he said. He said Ghana had revoked the instrument that permitted mining in forest reserves and strengthened efforts to combat illegal mining and environmental destruction. The Minister added that the government was pursuing land reclamation while supporting lawful small-scale miners to organise their operations, improve safety and adopt better mining methods. He identified the Responsible Cooperative Mining and Skills Development Programme as one of the initiatives aimed at promoting more responsible practices in the small-scale mining sector. “Our responsibility is to bring enforcement, opportunity, and restoration together,” he said. Mr Buah stressed that the country’s progress in managing its mineral resources should be assessed not only by the revenue generated from mining but also by the impact on the lives of people in mining communities. “A country cannot call a mining project successful if families are left without safe water or a future after the extraction of that mineral,” he said. The Minister said community development agreements, transparent oversight and credible environmental obligations are essential to ensuring that mining activities deliver lasting benefits to host communities. He noted that these measures are also important for building confidence in the mining sector and ensuring that companies fulfilled their responsibilities to communities and the environment. Mr Buah also assured investors, financiers, technology partners and international development institutions that Ghana was working to reform the governance of its mineral wealth and improve how its benefits were shared. He acknowledged that meaningful reforms required consultation, adjustment and patience, and called for constructive engagement from investors and development partners as the process continued. “I ask for your understanding and constructive engagement as this work moves forward. In return, we should expect clear rules, fair administration, open dialogue, and respect for lawful agreements. That is what Ghana stands for,” he said. The Minister added that mining investments needed to be commercially viable and capable of delivering reasonable returns, assuring partners that Ghana was prepared to work with them towards that objective. He stressed that Ghana’s approach to mineral development must balance investment and commercial viability with environmental responsibility, community welfare and accountability.

items.title: Un train de transport de voyageurs percute un camion à Bejaia : 18 blessés
items.description: Un train de transport de voyageurs a percuté un camion toupie ce lundi à Bejaia. L’accident a fait 18 blessés dont quatre ont été évacués à l’hôpital, a indiqué la Protection civile qui a mobilisé quatre ambulances et un camion d’intervention pour cette opération. Les blessés sont âgés entre 23 et 64 ans. La collision a eu lieu peu après 08 h 00 du matin à Bir Slam. Pour les raisons de cet accident, elles demeurent inconnues. La Société nationale des transports ferroviaires (SNTF) n’a pas communiqué sur cet accident. Dimanche, une personne a été mortellement percutée par un train à Sidi Bel Abbès. La victime a rendu l’âme sur les lieux de l’accident. L’article Un train de transport de voyageurs percute un camion à Bejaia : 18 blessés est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Cameroun : 700 places ouvertes pour le recrutement des étudiants en cycle doctorat
items.description: © DR Pour l’année académique 2026/ 2027, le gouvernement camerounais ouvre la procédure de sélection en cycle doctoral. A l’issue d’une réunion de la Commission nationale de la formation doctorale qu’il a présidée le 16 octobre, le ministre d’Etat ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur informe la communauté universitaire de l’autorisation d’ouverture des sélections dans les 11 universités d’Etat. Les quotas arrêtés indiquent que 700 places sont à pourvoir pour les nationaux. Elles sont reparties comme suit : 600 places pour les 11 universités d’Etat. 45 places au titre du quota spécial des médecins, odontostomatologues, pharmaciens salariés. 55 places au titre du quota spécial des chercheurs du ministère de la Recherche scientifique et de l’Innovation. A ces places réservées au nationaux, le quota des candidats internationaux s’élève à 115 places. Le total incluant les nationaux et les internationaux est de 815 places à pourvoir pour le compte de cette année. Dans sa communication, le ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur précise aussi les critères et le chronogramme des sélections. La sélection est ouverte aux étudiants titulaires de Master recherche ou équivalent obtenu avec une moyenne de 13/20 ou grade C+ minimum dans les sciences fondamentales ou 14/20 grade B dans les sciences humaines. Avoir obtenu une mention Assez bien dans l’un des trois niveaux du cycle licence au moins ; ne pas aller au rattrapage pour les évaluations des deux derniers semestres de Master. Le chronogramme prévoit que les chefs d’institutions universitaires lancent les appels à candidatures au plus tard le 24 octobre 2026. Puis ils vont transmettre les projets de listes de candidats sélectionnés au secrétariat technique de la Commission nationale de formation doctorale au plus tard le 30 novembre 2026. Les projets de listes seront acheminés en version physique et en version numérique. Cette sélection qui démarre marque la deuxième sélection suite à la décision du chef de l’Etat de renouer avec les sélections en cycle doctoral au Cameroun. Pour le compte de l’année 2025/2026, 600 candidats ont été sélectionnés pour poursuivre leurs études en thèse. Quotas fixés Cet article Cameroun : 700 places ouvertes pour le recrutement des étudiants en cycle doctorat est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: CAMES : Bangui lance le 23e concours d’agrégation de médecine
items.description: © DR Arrivée le 18 octobre 2026 à Bangui, la délégation du Secrétaire Général du CAMES, Pr Souleymane Konaté, a donné le coup d'envoi académique du 23ème Concours d'Agrégation de Médecine Humaine, Pharmacie, Odontostomatologie et Vétérinaire. Plus de 600 candidats attendus du 10 au 18 novembre 2026 en Centrafrique pour des épreuves. C'est un signal fort pour la Centrafrique et pour l'intégration universitaire africaine. Une délégation du Secrétariat général du Conseil Africain et Malgache pour l'Enseignement Supérieur (CAMES), conduite par son Secrétaire Général, le Professeur Souleymane Konaté, est arrivée à Bangui le 18 octobre 2026 pour le lancement académique du 23ème Concours d'Agrégation de Médecine Humaine, Pharmacie, Odontostomatologie, Médecine Vétérinaire et Productions Animales. Accueillie par le Président par intérim du Comité Consultatif Général du CAMES, Pr Gérard Gresenguet, le Président Coordonnateur des Jurys, Pr Boniface Koffi, et le point focal CAMES du pays, Dr Oscar Allahdin, la délégation a salué la mobilisation des plus Hautes Autorités centrafricaines. Au micro de la presse locale, le Pr Konaté, accompagné du Directeur des Programmes en charge des Concours, Pr Ali Doumma, a remercié Bangui pour l'accueil de ce prestigieux concours et rappelé l'enjeu : le lancement académique officiel aura lieu en ligne le lundi 19 octobre 2026 depuis l'Université de Bangui, avant les deuxième et troisième épreuves prévues du 10 au 18 novembre 2026. Plus de 600 candidats venus de tout l'espace CAMES sont attendus dans la capitale centrafricaine. Au-delà de l'excellence académique, ce concours est un instrument politique de souveraineté sanitaire, qui permet à l'Afrique de former elle-même ses Professeurs de médecine et de réduire sa dépendance aux expertises extérieures. Parmi les figures qui incarnent cette excellence figure le Professeur Vincent de Paul Djientcheu, éminent neurochirurgien camerounais et référence continentale. Président d'un jury de ce 23ème Concours, le Pr Djientcheu, ancien chef de service de neurochirurgie à Yaoundé et formateur de plusieurs générations de spécialistes, symbolise la montée en puissance de l'école médicale camerounaise au sein du CAMES. Sa présidence illustre la crédibilité et l'exigence scientifique que le Cameroun apporte à la certification des futurs agrégés. Pour Bangui, accueillir ce concours après des mois de préparation est aussi un succès diplomatique, qui confirme le retour de la Centrafrique sur la scène académique africaine. Cet article CAMES : Bangui lance le 23e concours d'agrégation de médecine est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: SHC dismisses state appeal against Mahrang's 2025 acquittal in sedition case
items.description: The Sindh High Court (SHC) on Monday dismissed an appeal filed by the provincial government through the prosecutor general against the acquittal of Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC) leader Mahrang Baloch in a sedition case, declaring it non-maintainable. Mahrang had been booked on terrorism and sedition charges by Malir district’s Quaidabad police on Oct 11, 2024 for allegedly inciting people by levelling “allegations against security institutions”. Over a year later, she was acquitted by a Karachi anti-terrorism court (ATC). Subsequently, acting prosecutor general Muntazir Mehdi, on behalf of the state, had challenged the acquittal before the SHC in December 2025. On Monday, a two-judge SHC bench, headed by Justice Shamsuddin Abbasi and including Justice Miran Muhammad Shah, heard the appeal. Advocate Jibran Nasir appeared before the court to represent Mahrang and advanced his arguments. The court observed that the complainant in the first information report (FIR) was a private individual and questioned how the prosecution could file an appeal against the acquittal instead of the complainant. The prosecution claimed that the ATC had ignored facts while accepting Mahrang’s acquittal application. It highlighted that the public prosecutor had informed the ATC that there was clear evidence against Mahrang and that such evidence was supposed to be presented during trial. The prosecution further argued that deciding the acquittal application before the framing of charges was inappropriate. Mahrang, who is in Quetta prison in connection with other cases, had filed an acquittal application under Section 265-K of the Code of Criminal Procedure before ATC-V, which the court allowed. The FIR was registered on the complaint of a resident named Asad Ali Shams, who claimed that Mahrang was inciting violence in his area. The FIR invoked Section 7 (punishment for acts of terrorism) of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) 1997 as well as sections 124-A (sedition), 148 (rioting, armed with deadly weapon), 149 (every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object), 153-A (promotion of enmity between groups), 500 (punishment for defamation) and 505 (statement conducing to public mischief) of the Pakistan Penal Code. In June, a Quetta ATC handed two life sentences to Mahrang and another BYC leader in a case involving the death of a security personnel during a 2024 protest in Gwadar. Mahrang’s challenge against her conviction is pending before the Balochistan High Court (BHC).

items.title: French prime minister calls for curfews as govt grapples with unrest
items.description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu called for localised curfews on Monday, as protesters blocked the entrance to the Louvre in Paris and authorities scrambled to stem public discontent that over the weekend saw mass cost-of-living demonstrations spill over into some of the worst street violence in recent years. Lecornu huddled with ministers in a crisis meeting after the interior minister said the police “had lost control” during the weekend’s unrest . With the Yellow Vests movement, which organised the weekend’s rallies, calling for a new round of protests next Saturday, Lecornu called for regional authorities to impose “partial” and “localised” curfews to protect businesses after hundreds of shops were damaged and looted. “I’m absolutely determined to restore public order,” he vowed, adding that the government was ready to impose a state of emergency “if needed”. Saturday’s demonstrations saw some half a million people turn out across France to protest the cost of living, but morphed into some of the worst violence to rock the country in years, with town halls and shops looted and set ablaze. French President Emmanuel Macron also refused Interior Minister Laurent Nunez’s resignation even as he acknowledged security and intelligence failures in the government response. More than 2,500 people were arrested, while almost 1,000 members of the security forces were injured. Injuries were also reported among protesters, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade. “On Saturday, in some major cities, you couldn’t look shopkeepers in the eye after hundreds of shops had been looted and tell them we hadn’t lost control,” Nunez said. Nunez acknowledged a “lack of anticipation” in the deployment of security forces on Saturday, whose numbers were insufficient to deal with the large crowds of rioters and looters on the fringes of the demonstrations. He estimated that some 60,000 law enforcement personnel had been deployed across the country that day. “Given the damage that has been caused, it was only right that I should hand in my resignation,” Nunez said. The presidency said in a statement that Macron had rejected the resignation, however, citing “the necessity for continued leadership of law enforcement”. Instead, Macron ordered Nunez to “take all necessary steps to ensure transparency over the failures in planning and intelligence that led to the violence”. To end the “barricades and looting, he also requested that the interior minister promptly implement new operational methods for security forces to use on the ground in combating rioters,” the statement added. Looting continued on Sunday, with Paris Mayor Emmanuel Gregoire saying Monday that around 30 shops had been targeted in the capital the previous day, describing the scenes as “unbearable”. CCTV footage shows a masked group breaking into a jewellery shop in Lyon, France, October 17, 2026, in this screengrab obtained from a handout video. — Reuters Nunez said some 350 people had been arrested in Paris on Sunday and overnight. Nationwide, more than 2,330 people were taken into police custody over the weekend — 70 per cent of whom were adults — and many of whom were already known to authorities, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said on Monday. More than 2,000 shops were expected to have been affected by the weekend’s violence across France, with damage running into “hundreds of millions of euros”, according to chamber of commerce president Alain Di Crescenzo. In an address to the nation on Sunday, Macron slammed the “unbridled” violence and said local authorities would be able to ban some rallies, but stopped short of imposing more drastic measures. City authorities in Marseille said on Monday they had banned public gatherings from noon to 08:00 pm (1000-1800 GMT). The European Union slammed the weekend violence as “unacceptable” but warned that the right to peaceful protest “must be protected” in France. Germany condemned the violence and updated its travel advice for France, saying “further demonstrations and, in some cases, further outbreaks of violence in the coming days cannot be ruled out”. The United Kingdom said the right to protest “can never excuse violence”. Louvre blocked Public discontent showed no signs of subsiding on Monday, with demonstrators blocking the entrance to Paris’s iconic Louvre Museum, the most visited in the world. Rising prices have fuelled anger in France, where diesel prices have jumped nearly 40pc and petrol by 25pc since March, and where food prices have risen by 25pc since 2021. The unrest has flared just months before a key presidential election where centrist Macron cannot stand again and Marine Le Pen, the far-right presidential candidate for the National Rally party, is riding high in the polls. Protesters and students from art and culture schools block the entrance to the Louvre Museum during a demonstration in support of a high school student movement demanding better school conditions and government action, in Paris, France, October 19, 2026. — Reuters Ministers and Le Pen have accused ultra-left groups of stoking the violence to boost the chances of the far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Melenchon in the presidential polls. On Monday, Lecornu blamed the “ultra-left movement” for seeking to “orchestrate deep unrest across the country”. “There is a whole network that could be mobilised to even call into question the timetable for the presidential election and the holding of the presidential election itself,” Lecornu told reporters. Europe Similar demonstrations have broken out in other countries. During the weekend, clashes broke out on the sidelines of a cost-of-living demonstration in Milan, with Mayor Giuseppe Sala warning: “I’m very worried because it’s a new phenomenon, which also originates from an international scenario and therefore feeds itself.” In Belgium, police fired tear gas and water cannons to disperse protesters in Brussels and Liege. In Spain, hundreds of tents have occupied Madrid’s central Puerta del Sol square since September, when the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her lifelong flat sparked nationwide protests in a country with soaring housing costs. Protesters have also set up tents in Portugal’s main cities of Lisbon and Porto over rising costs of housing.

items.title: Poor sanitation and menstrual stigma threaten girls’ dignity in rural Ghana – REEP Ghana
items.description: The Executive Director of REEP Ghana, Hairiya Bala, has decried the deplorable state of sanitation facilities and entrenched menstrual stigma that continue to strip girls and women, especially in rural Ghana, of their dignity and right to safe menstrual health management. She warned that the absence of adequate toilet facilities and limited access to essential hygiene materials demand massive investment in water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) infrastructure, coupled with sustained public education. The Executive Director issued the stark warning in Tamale during a menstrual dignity awareness campaign organized under the REEP Ghana Ambassadors on the Menstrual Cup Project. She insisted that menstruation must never be a source of humiliation and exclusion. “Menstruation is a natural phenomenon; however, stigma and shame continue to affect young girls and women, especially in rural communities,” she said. The campaign was designed to amplify the voices of young people, particularly girls, to openly confront menstrual health challenges while mobilizing boys and young men as allies in dismantling menstrual stigma. Ms. Bala maintained that robust community engagement and frank conversations are critical to demolishing dangerous myths surrounding menstruation and fostering an environment where girls and women can seek help without fear of ridicule or shaming. She called on the government, development partners, and traditional authorities to urgently prioritize investments in well-equipped toilet facilities, handwashing materials, and other essential WASH infrastructure to transform menstrual hygiene management in underserved communities. “Every young woman deserves to menstruate with dignity,” she emphasised. The campaign is part of the REEP Ghana Ambassadors on the Menstrual Cup Project, also known as the RAMCA project, implemented in partnership with 100% for the Children, with funding support from CISRA. The initiative seeks to bolster awareness on menstrual dignity, reshape public attitudes toward menstruation, and galvanize collective action to build safer, more supportive environments for girls and women.
